data.title: Quality Improvement - Refactoring

data.description:
## Problem statement

The audit runner's parent-first flow re-audits all children on every run because the freshness fingerprint includes the global git HEAD sha. In `--child-in-main-slot` mode, non-interactive runs leave all children with `partial` verdicts, which blocks the parent from recording a "Ready to close: Yes" result even when all parent ACs are met. This prevents audit completion for epics whose children were previously audited.

## Users

- **Audit runner / downtime worker** — expects a non-interactive audit of an epic to produce a valid verdict without requiring a live agent session.
- **Producer / human reviewer** — expects the audit to accurately reflect whether work is ready to close, not to block on stale or unserviced child verdicts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Fingerprint scoping.** `_compute_content_fingerprint` no longer includes the global git HEAD sha as a sole invalidation trigger; instead it is scoped to child-relevant key files and/or commits so that unrelated HEAD movement on `dev` does not invalidate previously valid child audits.
- **AC2 — In-main-slot partial verdict handling.** When a child's `ac_results` remain `partial` because the invoking agent session never serviced the `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items, the parent audit treats those verdicts as "not assessed" (inherits the child's previously stored verdict or marks them reusable) rather than blocking the parent's readiness-to-close decision.
- **AC3 — Diagnostic clarity.** The audit output surfaces a clear, machine-parseable diagnostic that distinguishes a "child partial because unserviced in-main-slot" verdict from a genuine "not-ready" child verdict, including the reason code in the audit summary.
- **AC4 — No regression on interactive runs.** The above fixes do not change the behaviour of interactive audit runs (where an agent session *can* service in-main-slot items); those continue to honour the full in-main-slot workflow.
- **AC5 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.** Run the complete suite and confirm zero failures.

## Constraints

- The fix must not introduce a new mode flag or require operator configuration; it should be the default behaviour.
- The fix should be backward-compatible with persisted audit results (old fingerprint format should still be readable).
- The change scope is the audit runner's child freshness logic (`_compute_content_fingerprint`, `_child_content_changed`), the in-main-slot verdict accumulation logic (`_build_issue_json`, `all_ac_acceptable`), and the diagnostic output path.

## Existing state

- `_compute_content_fingerprint` includes the current git HEAD sha — any new commit on `dev` invalidates every stored child audit.
- In `child_in_main_slot=True` mode, child Phase-1 AC screens and Phase-2 deep analysis emit `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items for the invoking session. In non-interactive runs, these are never serviced and stay `partial`.
- `_build_issue_json` includes child AC verdicts in `all_ac_acceptable`, so the parent is reported "Ready to close: No" even when all parent ACs are met.
- The runner's terminal lifecycle then demotes parent and children to `open`/`plan_complete` as a side effect.

## Desired change

1. **Scope the fingerprint**: Replace the global HEAD sha in `_compute_content_fingerprint` with a child-scoped hash (key files + relevant commits).
2. **Handle partial verdicts**: When computing `all_ac_acceptable`, skip children whose verdict is `partial` due to unserviced in-main-slot items — treat them as "not assessed" rather than "not accepted."
3. **Add diagnostics**: In the audit summary, emit a reason code or flag indicating when a child's `partial` verdict is due to unserviced in-main-slot items vs. genuine assessment failure.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/audit/` or equivalent audit runner module — `_compute_content_fingerprint`, `_child_content_changed`, `_build_issue_json`, in-main-slot verdict handling
- `scripts/audit_runner*` or equivalent — runner invocation, non-interactive path
- Audit output/summary formatter — diagnostic message generation

## Related work

- **AH-0MUD8E015004C4JO** — Unify PlayScene/GymFormationScene combat logic (completed): the parent epic that discovered this issue during audit.
- **SA-0MSKB6VJA005N43F** — Audit parent-first flow (internal assertion): the flow that triggers the re-audit on stale children.
- **SA-0MT2XRGEU0009QRE** — Audit in-main-slot mode (internal assertion): the mode that creates `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` items.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — fingerprint scoping is incomplete.** If child-relevant files/commits are not correctly identified, stale audits may still be invalidated or, conversely, genuinely stale audits may be reused. Mitigation: carefully identify the key files that each child audit covers; add a test case that simulates unrelated HEAD movement vs. child-relevant HEAD movement.
- **Risk — inheriting stale child verdicts masks real regressions.** If a child's code changed but the fingerprint didn't catch it, inheriting an old verdict is incorrect. Mitigation: the fingerprint scoping should cover all files relevant to the child audit.
- **Assumption:** all three suggested directions are desired (fingerprint scoping, partial-verdict handling, diagnostic clarity).
- **Assumption:** the audit runner is a Node.js/TypeScript or Python tool within the project; the fix applies to the runner's Python/TS source.
data.title: Audit: parent-first flow re-audits stale children and blocks on unserviced in-main-slot verdicts

## Summary

`skill/plan/plan_helpers.py::plan-approval-gate` fails to request producer approval for items whose effort is a t-shirt size (XS/S/M/L/XL) or whose risk is `Severe`. The skill contract states "Absent effort/risk → default conservatively to requesting approval (a human checkpoint is never silently skipped)" and the gate should request approval for the largest/highest-risk items — but the vocabulary sets did not match the values `wl` actually stores, so a Severe-risk item could silently skip the human checkpoint.

Discovered during planning of **SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX** (effort `M`, risk `Severe`): the gate returned `request_approval: false`, so a Severe-risk security/data-loss item would have silently skipped the human checkpoint. The plan session escalated manually instead.

**discovered-from:SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX**

## Superseded acceptance criteria (SA-0MUYG0HE6001YTEM)

The original fix targeted an **OR** gate (approval when effort M/L/XL OR risk High/Severe). After this item was filed, **SA-0MUYG0HE6001YTEM** ("Tighten plan-approval-gate to largest and highest risk only", shipped v0.1.21) changed the gate to an **AND** gate: approval only when effort **Extra Large** AND risk **High/Severe**. **SA-0MV85VT250096CTY** then added effort-label normalisation (`XL` ↔ `Extra Large`). The acceptance criteria below are therefore restated against the currently-shipped contract. Under the AND gate the original `M`/`Severe` example now correctly does **not** trigger approval.

## Evidence

- `wl show SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX --json` → `"effort": "M"`, `"risk": "Severe"`.
- `python3 skill/plan/plan_helpers.py plan-approval-gate SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX` → `{"request_approval": false, ...}`.
- `wl update --help` canonical vocabularies: effort `XS,S,M,L,XL`; risk `Low,Medium,High,Severe`.
- Remaining genuine gaps after the AND-gate supersession: (a) a value that is present but **unrecognised** (outside the canonical vocabulary) silently skipped the checkpoint (only absent values defaulted to approval); (b) `resolve_complexity_tier` omitted `Severe` from its risk scale and did not normalise abbreviated effort — the gap explicitly deferred here by SA-0MUYG0HE6001YTEM.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `plan-approval-gate` returns `request_approval: true` for effort `XL`/`Extra Large` **AND** risk `High`/`Severe` (the currently-shipped AND contract, SA-0MUYG0HE6001YTEM); `M`/`L` no longer trigger approval by themselves.
- [ ] Both t-shirt abbreviations and full words are accepted for effort (`XL` ↔ `Extra Large`) at the gate.
- [ ] Absent **or unrecognised** effort/risk defaults conservatively to requesting approval (a human checkpoint is never silently skipped).
- [ ] Unit tests cover the full effort × risk matrix, the abbreviation/full-label parity matrix, the `M`/`Severe` non-triggering case from SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX, and the unrecognised-value conservative default.
- [ ] `resolve_complexity_tier` recognises `Severe` (ranks above `High`) and normalises abbreviated effort (the gap deferred here by SA-0MUYG0HE6001YTEM).

**Key Files:**
- skill/plan/plan_helpers.py
- skill/plan/tests/test_plan_helpers.py
data.title: plan-approval-gate skips checkpoint for t-shirt effort and Severe risk

# Repair wl sync for the operator's GitHub-identity checkout

`discovered-from:SA-0MV9J471W002LCE1` (created during that item's session; actioned by operator directive).

## Problem statement

`wl sync` in this checkout cannot merge incoming worklog data: the author-identity
gate (SA-0MUJ2VMF7000UHCX) refuses all remote `refs/worklog/data` commits because
they are authored by `250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com` (the operator's
GitHub identity) while the local checkout's `user.email` is `pi@local`. Additional
blockers are 31 incident-era commits from the leaked-`GIT_DIR` incident
(2026-09-26) authored as `t@t.com` — a hardcoded `INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS` sentinel
that must NOT be whitelisted.

## Existing state

- `.worklog/config.yaml` previously had no `syncAllowedAuthors` — the gate had
  only the strict user.email comparison.
- `refs/worklog/data` history contains 31 contiguous `t@t.com` commits
  (positions `345ea154a..fbf0b5bda`, 2026-09-26) that the gate must keep refusing.
- `wl sync` therefore could not merge or push (`1559 incoming commit(s) fail the
  author-identity gate`; after whitelisting the operator identity: `31`).

## Desired change

1. Add the operator's GitHub noreply email to `syncAllowedAuthors` in
   `.worklog/config.yaml` so legitimate operator-identity commits pass the gate.
2. Purge the 31 incident-era `t@t.com` commits from `refs/worklog/data` history
   (re-parent past the block without changing any tree content), so the gate has
   nothing to refuse.
3. `wl sync` completes and pushes the current SQLite store (incl. SA-0MV9J471W002LCE1).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1:** `wl sync --dry-run` no longer refuses on author identity.
2. **AC2:** `wl sync` completes successfully (merge + push), and
   `SA-0MV9J471W002LCE1` appears in `refs/worklog/data`.
3. **AC3:** No `t@t.com`-authored commits remain on `refs/worklog/data`.
4. **AC4:** `t@t.com` is NOT added to `syncAllowedAuthors` (sentinel emails stay
   refused — the quarantine is preserved).
5. **AC5:** The final `refs/worklog/data` tree is identical to the pre-purge tree
   (verified via `git diff`, plus work item count preserved).

## Key Files

- `.worklog/config.yaml` — `syncAllowedAuthors` allow-list entry.
- `refs/worklog/data` — incident-block purge (git history rewrite).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: force-push history rewrite on a shared branch.** Mitigation: the rewrite
  only re-parents the post-block linear history; trees are untouched; the loss of
  31 incident-erа commits is the intended quarantine. Any clone that fast-forwards
  is unaffected; others receive the rewritten chain on their next fetch.
- **Assumption:** `t@t.com` commits carry no legitimate post-incident data (they
  are in the 2026-09-26 incident window, superseded by the 2026-09-27+
  operator-identity snapshots).
data.title: Repair wl sync: allow operator GitHub identity, purge incident-era t@t.com commits from worklog branch

Discovered-from:SA-0MUJQ5BPF001PICU.

## Summary

`wl sync` refuses to merge inbound worklog commits on refs/worklog/data: 4 commits (66b8e59b, a31dfb9a, 664d5b55, 1afacea2) authored `Sorra the Orc <pi@local>` (2026-10-15) fail the author gate — `pi@local` does not match configured `user.email` (`250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com`) and is not in `syncAllowedAuthors`.

This blocks pushing the local close of SA-0MUJQ5BPF001PICU (and any other local worklog mutations) to origin. Local DB update succeeded; only remote sync is blocked.

## Verified state (2026-10-16 plan session)

- Exactly 4 gating commits, all `pi@local`, after last-synced-ref `9727585074`: `66b8e59b`, `a31dfb9a`, `664d5b55`, `1afacea2` (verified via `git log 97275850..refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data`).
- Gate semantics (worklog package `sync.js::checkAuthorIdentity`): a commit passes if author email matches `user.email` OR is in `syncAllowedAuthors`. Empty-email gate is never bypassed.
- 3 older `pi@local` commits (2026-09-16) predate last-synced-ref and are not gating.
- Main-checkout identity is healthy (`check_git_identity.py` → ok); the offending pushes came from a pi session with unset/incorrect identity.
- Stranded data is real: e.g. SA-0MV9JVLBQ0090RNC (the earlier config fix) is absent from the local store.

## Decisions (operator, 2026-10-16)

- **Remediation of the 4 stranded commits:** one-time operator-authorized `wl sync --allow-foreign-author` (option a) — the designed escape hatch; no shared-history rewrite; the subsequent correctly-authored push advances last-synced-ref past the offenders.
- **Recurrence prevention:** add `pi@local` to `syncAllowedAuthors` in `.worklog/config.yaml` for this project (operator-chosen option c), so pi-session-authored sync commits pass the gate. This deliberately widens the project gate to accept `pi@local` (empty-email gate still enforced); the general guard `scripts/check_git_identity.py` must NOT be hardened to flag `pi@local` (that would contradict the allow-list).

## Goal

Restore `wl sync` so local worklog mutations push to origin, and prevent recurrence of author-identity refusals for pi-session commits.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1** `wl sync` completes without an author-identity refusal, and previously-stranded items (e.g. SA-0MV9JVLBQ0090RNC) are present in the local store; `last-synced-ref` advances past the 4 offending commits.
- [ ] **AC2** The one-time `--allow-foreign-author` remediation is operator-authorized and recorded in a comment with the exact command and output (safety-gate provenance).
- [ ] **AC3** `pi@local` is added to `syncAllowedAuthors` in `.worklog/config.yaml` (project scope), and a regression test pins that the config allow-list accepts a `pi@local`-authored commit while an arbitrary foreign email is still refused.
- [ ] **AC4** Full test suite passes on a clean build; all changes committed with work-item association.

## Plan (approved 2026-10-16; 3 children, test-first)

1. **Author-gate incident regression tests** (test-first) — drive the gate/guard decision for the `pi@local` allow-list change; red before, green after.
2. **Recover stranded worklog data** (operator-authorized) — one-time `wl sync --allow-foreign-author`, verify stranded items present, last-synced-ref advances.
3. **Add `pi@local` to syncAllowedAuthors** (project allow-list) — `.worklog/config.yaml` change + docs note, depends on 1.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which remediation for the 4 stranded commits — (a) one-time authorized `wl sync --allow-foreign-author`, (b) rewrite the 4 authors and force-update refs/worklog/data, or (c) add `pi@local` to syncAllowedAuthors?" — Answer (operator, 2026-10-16): "(a)". Final: one-time authorized `--allow-foreign-author` merge; no history rewrite. Rationale: designed escape hatch, no shared-ref rewrite.
- Q: "Scope of recurrence prevention — (i) harden `check_git_identity.py` to flag `pi@local` + document, (ii) additionally enforce identity at pi-session/worktree setup, (iii) defer?" — Answer (operator, 2026-10-16): "Add pi@local to the allow list for this project". Final: option (c) from the remediation list — add `pi@local` to `syncAllowedAuthors` in `.worklog/config.yaml`; do NOT harden the guard. Note: this intentionally widens the gate for this project (empty-email gate still never bypassed).
data.title: wl sync blocked: inbound worklog commits authored pi@local fail the author-identity gate

Discovered-from:SA-0MVB57M02008QPJS.

## Goal

Pin the resolved author-identity-gate behaviour with hermetic automated tests, so the `pi@local` sync block (SA-0MVB57M02008QPJS) cannot silently regress.

## Background

SA-0MVB57M02008QPJS decisions (operator-approved): (1) one-time `--allow-foreign-author` merge; (2) add `pi@local` to `syncAllowedAuthors` in `.worklog/config.yaml` (project scope). The gate (`/usr/local/lib/node_modules/worklog/dist/sync.js::checkAuthorIdentity`) accepts a commit author when it matches `user.email` or is in `syncAllowedAuthors`; the empty-email gate is never bypassed.

Tests must assert the *new* intended contract: `pi@local` in the allow-list passes the gate, while an arbitrary foreign email (e.g. `evil@example.com`) is still refused and an empty author email is always refused.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1** A hermetic test pins that adding `pi@local` to the project's allow-list makes the config allow-list accept a `pi@local`-authored commit while an arbitrary foreign email is still refused (drives the author-gate decision via the worklog package's exported `checkAuthorIdentity`/config helpers, or a faithful decision reimplementation over the parsed `syncAllowedAuthors` config).
- [ ] **AC2** The test reads the project's real `.worklog/config.yaml` and asserts `syncAllowedAuthors` contains both `pi@local` and the canonical GitHub identity (`250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com`) — red before the config change (`Add pi@local to syncAllowedAuthors`) lands, green after.
- [ ] **AC3** Tests are hermetic: no live remote/git-network, no real `wl sync`, lone test fixtures under tmp.

- [ ] **AC4** Full test suite passes on a clean build; all changes committed with work-item association.

## Key Files

- `.worklog/config.yaml` (read-only fixture in test)
- `tests/` (new test module, e.g. `tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py`)

## Dependencies

- Blocked-by: SA-0MVB57M02008QPJS (parent). No other prereqs.

## Deliverables

- Test module(s) + comment with red/green evidence.
